records.rationale: Natural estimate-how-much instruction about a personal past purchase.

records.originalText: No matter where you may go, don't forget to write to me.
records.finalText: No matter where you may go, don't forget to write to me.
records.rationale: Natural formal no-matter-where concession with a reminder.

records.originalText: What is it that makes you think that way?
records.finalText: What is it that makes you think that way?
records.rationale: Natural emphatic cleft question about someone's reasoning.

records.originalText: I'm surprised at your behavior.
records.finalText: I'm surprised at your behavior.
records.rationale: Natural personal reaction with surprised at.

records.originalText: It is outrageous that you should spend so much money.
records.finalText: It is outrageous that you should spend so much money.
records.rationale: Natural formal evaluative should after outrageous, about a particular expense.

records.originalText: It is a pity that you should lose such a chance.
records.finalText: It is a pity that you should lose such a chance.
records.rationale: Natural formal evaluative should about losing an opportunity.

records.originalText: It is foolish of you to believe such a thing.
records.finalText: It is foolish of you to believe such a thing.
records.rationale: Grammatical evaluation of a specific belief, rather than an identity-based insult.

records.originalText: It makes no difference to me whether you believe it or not.
records.finalText: It makes no difference to me whether you believe it or not.
records.rationale: Natural personal indifference expression with whether-or-not belief.

records.originalText: It makes little difference to me whether you believe it or not.
records.finalText: It makes little difference to me whether you believe it or not.
records.rationale: Near-paraphrase of the selected indifference-to-belief statement.

records.originalText: The time will come when you'll regret it.
records.finalText: The time will come when you'll regret it.
records.rationale: Natural future temporal relative clause about a possible regret.

records.originalText: When was it that you visited the museum?
records.finalText: When was it that you visited the museum?
records.rationale: Natural emphatic cleft question about a museum visit.

records.originalText: It is no wonder that you are turning down the proposal.
records.finalText: It is no wonder that you are turning down the proposal.
records.rationale: Natural no-wonder expression with turn down a proposal.

records.originalText: What made it difficult for you to carry out the plan?
records.finalText: What made it difficult for you to carry out the plan?
records.rationale: Natural make-it-difficult causative question and carry out a plan.

records.originalText: It is absolutely necessary that you be at the meeting.
records.finalText: It is absolutely necessary that you be at the meeting.
records.rationale: Natural formal mandative be after absolutely necessary.

records.originalText: There are a good many reasons why you shouldn't do it.
records.finalText: There are a good many reasons why you shouldn't do it.
records.rationale: Natural a-good-many quantifier with a relative reason clause.

records.originalText: We will pay you according to the amount of work you do.
records.finalText: We will pay you according to the amount of work you do.
records.rationale: Natural generic pay-by-amount-of-work agreement; no product, wage-rate or real employment advice.

records.originalText: I'm glad you enjoy skiing, but I guess it's just not my cup of tea.
records.finalText: I'm glad you enjoy skiing, but I guess it's just not my cup of tea.
records.rationale: Conventional not-my-cup-of-tea preference idiom with a polite contrast.

records.originalText: It is dangerous for you to swim in this river.
records.finalText: It is dangerous for you to swim in this river.
records.rationale: Natural generic water-safety warning without unsafe procedural detail.

records.originalText: The time will come when you will understand this.
records.finalText: The time will come when you will understand this.
records.rationale: Natural personal prediction with a future time-relative clause.

records.originalText: Where was it that you found this key?
records.finalText: Where was it that you found this key?
records.rationale: Natural emphatic cleft question about finding an object.

records.originalText: There is no need for you to stay here.
records.finalText: There is no need for you to stay here.
records.rationale: Natural no-need-for-you infinitive expressing lack of necessity.

records.originalText: My life would be completely empty without you.
records.finalText: My life would be completely empty without you.
records.rationale: Natural personal hypothetical emotion with a without-phrase.

records.originalText: Have you ever seen Mt. Fuji? It is beautiful beyond description.
records.finalText: Have you ever seen Mount Fuji? It is beautiful beyond description.
records.rationale: Expand Mt. to Mount for self-contained wording; preserve the subjective scenic appreciation.

records.originalText: Repetition helps you remember something.
records.finalText: Repetition helps you remember something.
records.rationale: Familiar qualified learning observation using helps rather than guaranteeing retention.

records.originalText: Chestnuts have to be boiled for at least fifteen minutes.
records.finalText: Chestnuts have to be boiled for at least fifteen minutes.
records.rationale: Unqualified mandatory chestnut cooking time lacks preparation/recipe context.

records.originalText: There is a hole in your sock.
records.finalText: There is a hole in your sock.
records.rationale: Simple clothing condition statement with everyday vocabulary.

records.originalText: Put on your shoes. Let's go out for dinner.
records.finalText: Put on your shoes. Let's go out for dinner.
records.rationale: Coherent two-sentence dressing instruction and dinner suggestion.

records.originalText: Before buying shoes, you should try them on.
records.finalText: Before buying shoes, you should try them on.
records.rationale: Natural before-plus-gerund advice with try shoes on.

records.originalText: Please remove your shoes before entering the house.
records.finalText: Please remove your shoes before entering the house.
records.rationale: Common polite footwear request with a time clause.

records.originalText: The soles of my shoes are worn.
records.finalText: The soles of my shoes are worn.
records.rationale: Natural footwear description with soles and worn.

records.originalText: Your feet are swollen because your shoes are too small.
records.finalText: Your feet are swollen because your shoes are too small.
records.rationale: Unverified causal diagnosis of swelling from shoe size lacks appropriate medical context.

records.originalText: Please remove the mud from your shoes.
records.finalText: Please remove the mud from your shoes.
records.rationale: Natural practical request with remove and common material/location nouns.

records.originalText: I would rather die than live in dishonor.
records.finalText: I would rather die than live in dishonor.
records.rationale: Romanticized preference for death over dishonor is unnecessary for this general learner packet.

records.originalText: I found the book by accident.
records.finalText: I found the book by accident.
records.rationale: Natural past discovery with by accident.

records.originalText: Judging from the look of the sky, it will clear up in the afternoon.
records.finalText: Judging from the look of the sky, it will clear up in the afternoon.
records.rationale: Natural explicitly inferred weather prediction from a fictional speaker, not a real forecast.

records.originalText: Our house was robbed while we were away.
records.finalText: Our house was robbed while we were away.
records.rationale: Recognizable colloquial personal property-crime narrative with a while-clause.

records.originalText: Fill in the blanks with suitable words.
records.finalText: Fill in the blanks with suitable words.
records.rationale: Common complete language-learning instruction using fill in the blanks.

records.originalText: The airport was closed because of the fog.
records.finalText: The airport was closed because of the fog.
records.rationale: Natural past passive cause statement about fog and an airport.

records.originalText: There were a great many people at the airport.
records.finalText: There were a great many people at the airport.
records.rationale: Natural a-great-many quantifier in a past existential sentence.

records.originalText: What time should I go to the airport?
records.finalText: What time should I go to the airport?
records.rationale: Practical modal question about travel timing.

records.originalText: Please pick me up at the airport at five.
records.finalText: Please pick me up at the airport at five.
records.rationale: Common polite pickup request with a place and spelled-out time.

records.originalText: Please tell me which railway line to use from the airport to downtown.
records.finalText: Please tell me which railway line to use from the airport to downtown.
records.rationale: Clear travel request with an embedded which-line question.

records.originalText: Is there a shuttle bus between the hotel and airport?
records.finalText: Is there a shuttle bus between the hotel and airport?
records.rationale: Natural existential question about shuttle-bus service between two generic places.

records.originalText: Oxygen from the air dissolves in water.
records.finalText: Oxygen from the air dissolves in water.
records.rationale: Stable basic physical description of oxygen dissolving in water.

records.originalText: Because of the problem of air pollution, the bicycle may some day replace the automobile.
records.finalText: Because of the problem of air pollution, the bicycle may some day replace the automobile.
records.rationale: Grammatical speculative environmental future with may, rather than a current trend assertion.

records.originalText: Air is a mixture of gases that we cannot see.
records.finalText: Air is a mixture of gases that we cannot see.
records.rationale: Stable basic description of air with a relative clause about invisible gases.

records.originalText: Air is a mixture of several gases.
records.finalText: Air is a mixture of several gases.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the air-mixture definition already selected, with less descriptive information.
